title: Resilience handoff and retry playbook retro
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on followup from last week's intermittent 502/504 spike. Team walked through timeline, hypothesized causes (hot keys + bursty traffic + insufficient warm KV cache), tuned client retry windows and rate-windowing, agreed on two service-side mitigations and a customer-side retry spec. Next: Redwood to run small targeted load test, Atlas to instrument backoff and share traces, schedule security doc delivery.
action_items: Theo Yang | run targeted 20m load test with 90th,% tail latency profile and attach perf traces | 2027-05-17
Lina Park | add client-side jittered exponential backoff per proposed spec and push to staging | 2027-05-20
Mara Jenkins | share updated retry-playbook doc and security questionnaire link | 2027-05-15
Carlos Vega | open support ticket for dedicated KV cache profiling and include correlation IDs | 2027-05-16
next_steps: Redwood -> provide trimmed latency trace and enriched logs from the 2027-05-11 incident
Atlas -> deploy client retry patch to staging and report 1h of telemetry
Joint -> 30-minute follow-up after tests to confirm whether fallback routing is needed
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14 09:30 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Mara Jenkins (Redwood AE), Theo Yang (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM), Lina Park (Atlas SRE), Omar Ruiz (Atlas Platform), Priya Menon (Atlas CTO), Samir Desai (Atlas Security)

[00:00] Mara: hey, everyone, thanks for joining. we have 46 minutes on the clock, quick agenda — incident recap, mitigation steps we tried, tuning the retry windows, and action handoff. sound good?
[00:16] Lina: yep that works — we want to make sure the 5xxs don't recur during our peak batch jobs on friday.
[00:22] Omar: also we need to verify that the tenant isolation knobs are doing what we expect, last time we saw cross-tenant burst effects.
[00:30] Theo: quick housekeeping — i'll share a short repro plan and a lightweight load harness, it's not the full perf suite but enough to repro the hotkey behaviour we suspect.
[00:38] Priya: ok, but before we go deep, can you summarize what you saw on the 11th? our pager went off, but our SREs didn't have a clear root cause.
[00:46] Mara: sure. brief timeline: around 02:12 UTC we started seeing elevated 502 and 504s for roughly 20 minutes, spike in tail latency, token service timeouts. Redwood observed increased queuing on a subset of nodes serving the LLM variant. correlation with a small number of prompt families that are hot (lots of similar prefix) — so hot key plus sudden concurrent jobs.
[01:10] Samir: on our side, auth and network looked fine, no changes to firewall or VPC routes. we did note a parallel increase in embedding requests at the same time.
[01:20] Theo: yes, embedding batch and generation requests overlapped. suspect that KV cache coldness meant more packs were loading from disk / cold pages, leading to transient CPU / mem pressure. also some clients were retrying too aggressively which amplified the tail.
[01:36] Lina: when you say "KV cache coldness" do you mean the k v cache wasn't populated? we thought the warmup policy would keep it hot between jobs.
[01:44] Theo: correct — the warmup depends on steady prefix overlap. the batch jobs were a burst after a quiet window; the cache TTL + eviction plus model variant churn meant the working set wasn't fully resident. the runtime then paid a cost shuffling pages.
[01:58] Omar: got it. so what's the immediate mitigation? we patched client retries last time but we still saw some 5xxs.
[02:06] Mara: there were two levers we applied: server-side rate-windowing (to smooth burst admission) and a temporary fallback policy that routed high-latency requests to a smaller, cheaper model so the critical paths stayed alive. that helped but didn't eliminate the tail.
[02:24] Priya: the fallback to smaller model changed output quality though — we need to understand SLA vs quality tradeoff.
[02:30] Theo: agreed. fallback is last resort; prefer preventing amplification. so client-side backoff + smarter admission should be first.
[02:38] Lina: our client retries were a fixed 1s backoff x4, no jitter. we pushed a fix to jitter, but we didn't change the max attempts.
[02:47] Mara: that aligns with what we saw — synchronized retries caused a retry-storm that hit the same hot nodes.
[02:54] Omar: can you recommend a client retry spec? we need something we can ship to the client libs team.
[02:59] Theo: yes. proposed spec: immediate 100-200ms first retry only for idempotent calls, then jittered exponential backoff starting at 500ms, multiplier 2, max attempts 3 for generation calls. introduce per-route retry budgets and fail-fast on 429/503 depending on header flags. I'll produce a one-pager.
[03:20] Lina: also propose we use a jitter window of +- 250ms and add random seed in clients so not all instances retry the same tick.
[03:28] Samir: sounds good, but security wants to ensure retries don't leak sensitive traces or increase retention requirements.
[03:34] Samir: our compliance needs a mapping of what is logged and for how long.
[03:38] Carlos: i can coordinate the security doc handoff — Mara, we'll attach the minimal-logs guidance.
[03:44] Mara: i'll share the security questionnaire link and the limited-telemetry guidelines after the call.
[03:49] Priya: great. another question, you mentioned admission controls — can you explain rate-windowing?
[03:55] Theo: rate-windowing is a sliding-per-tenant window that limits the number of inflight requests admitted to the hot path over small intervals, say 1s windows. it smooths bursts by queuing or rejecting requests before they reach the model runtime. we have two modes: soft queuing (delays) and hard reject (return 429) — we can tailor per-tenant.
[04:17] Omar: do we need Dedicated to get per-tenant guarantees? we're on hosted now.
[04:22] Mara: you can get some of the benefits in hosted via per-tenant windowing and routing, but Dedicated gives isolation at instance level — less noisy neighbor risk. it's a tradeoff for cost.
[04:30] Priya: we'll weigh that, but first let's fix the retry/queue behavior.
[04:35] Lina: question on tracing: when you ran your internal correlations, what IDs should we preserve on our side so we can join logs?
[04:42] Theo: include request_id, client_instance_id, and route_name. if you can surface client-side retry attempt number that helps. we'll also add a short correlation header we can honor on Redwood side.
[04:53] Lina: ok we'll add that.
[04:56] Mara: quick demo — (screen share) here's the timeline from our side for the 11th: you can see latency climb, and at 02:13 we started queue spillover.
[05:12] Omar: hm, i see a cluster of similar prompt prefixes — that's the hot key. can you annotate which requests hit the cached KV vs cold-load path?
[05:21] Theo: we have flags but they are sometimes inconsistent in the auto-trace — will add an explicit cold_load boolean in traces.
[05:29] Priya: that will help. also metrics wise, can you expose the per-node eviction counts? we want to correlate with memory pressure.
[05:37] Theo: yes, we can surface eviction_per_min metric and a rough resident_set_size gauge.
[05:43] Lina: about the fallback to smaller model — did you observe any pattern where the fallback flapped back and forth? we saw some flapping.
[05:50] Theo: flapping happened because the routing policy tried to return to the primary as soon as latency dropped; but if the cache wasn't warm yet, it would bounce. We need hysteresis — a cooldown window before reverting traffic.
[06:03] Mara: agreed. add cooldown of ~5 minutes to avoid oscillation.
[06:08] Omar: that seems long for some flows but safe. can that be per-route?
[06:12] Theo: yes per-route cooldowns are supported.
[06:15] Priya: ok, the action plan then — client retry spec, server-side rate-windowing + hysteresis, targeted load test, improved trace headers.
[06:23] Mara: I'll recap later. now, quick Q&A on security — Samir?
[06:29] Samir: two things: KMS integration for customer keys, and audit log retention. for the POC we prefer a short retention but we need to ensure we can escalate to 90 days for prod. what's Redwood's stance?
[06:40] Mara: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (we call it KMS/HSM) on Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports envelope encryption with managed keys; we can map options in the security doc. retention is configurable with enterprise add-on.
[06:52] Samir: ok please include SSO/SAML integration notes and SOC2 artifact reference.
[06:57] Carlos: will do.
[07:00] Lina: back to reliability, if we implement the proposed client retry changes and the rate-windowing, what residual risk do we expect?
[07:09] Theo: residual is mostly cold-start windows for very rare prefixes and extremely high concurrency bursts. mitigations: pre-warm for scheduled jobs, prefix-aware cache warmup, and adaptive batching.
[07:21] Omar: pre-warm seems attractive for our nightly batch jobs — can Redwood accept a pre-warm signal?
[07:27] Mara: yes, we can expose a private pre-warm API to seed the KV cache for a given model/prefix set. we'll need a small contract on volume and time.
[07:36] Priya: we'll prototype that.
[07:39] Samir: one more security note, when you do fallback to smaller model, ensure that the contract about telemetry and content redaction is respected; smaller model might be hosted differently.
[07:50] Theo: good call — we'll include model-hosting flags in the trace to indicate hosting mode.
[07:56] Mara: ok i'm going to list immediate deliverables: theo will run a short load test and share artifacts, lina will roll client jitter, mara will push docs. any objections?
[08:06] Lina: none.
[08:08] Omar: none.
[08:10] (brief cross talk, typing)
[08:20] Theo: quick detail on load test: i'll aim for 20 minutes at 2x normal peak concurrency with a mix of generation and embedding traffic, include a hotkey prefix set and cold prefixes. expected output: tail latencies, node-level perf counters, and a heatmap of KV misses.
[08:36] Mara: perfect. will you include a step where you toggle rate-windowing to show differences?
[08:41] Theo: yes, two runs — with and without windowing.
[08:44] Lina: we'll provide a short sample of our prompt prefix sets, but privacy note: strip customer PII.
[08:51] Priya: on deployment timeline, we want these client changes in staging by end of week, and the follow-up sync monday next week. is that feasible?
[08:59] Mara: yes — theo and i can coordinate.
[09:03] Carlos: i'll open a calendar invite for monday 2027-05-17 14:00 UTC for the follow-up.
[09:09] Priya: perfect.
[09:11] Samir: one question about metrics — can you expose retry-attempt counts per-client-id so we can detect if a patch works?
[09:19] Theo: yes, retry_attempts_by_client and retry_success_by_client are available, we'll add them to the dashboard.
[09:26] Lina: thanks. small nit — please don't surface internal node ids to our logs, use role-based names.
[09:32] Mara: noted. we'll obfuscate node ids in shared artifacts.
[09:36] Omar: last item — cost. if we do fallback routing more often, what's the cost delta? we need an estimate for budget.
[09:44] Mara: fallback to a smaller model is typically 30-60% cheaper per-token, but with potentially lower quality. i can provide a cost delta table per model variant and per-token rates.
[09:55] Priya: please do. finance will want that before any long-term decision.
[09:59] (short pause)
[10:05] Mara: ok, recap of next steps out loud: theo runs load tests and shares traces by 2027-05-17; lina deploys jittered backoff and reports telemetry by 2027-05-20; mara shares retry-playbook and security doc by 2027-05-15; follow-up 30m sync on monday 2027-05-17 14:00 UTC.
[10:29] Lina: confirmed.
[10:31] Omar: confirmed.
[10:33] Priya: thanks all. appreciate the quick turnaround.
[10:36] Mara: thanks everyone, we'll do the handoffs. end call.

Notes: transcription contains minor errors in acronyms (SAML sometimes transcribed as 'S A M L'), occasional speaker label swaps early in the call due to joins. Logs/attachments referenced: "2027-05-11-incident-timeline.png" (Redwood link), "atlas-prefix-sample.json" (Atlas internal), "retry-playbook-draft-v2.pdf" (Redwood).
